**Brex pricing** starts at $0 per user a month for Essentials, $12 per user for Premium, and custom quotes for Enterprise, as listed on November 11, 2026. Capital One has owned Brex since April 7, 2026.


The harder question is what your company will pay. A $0 plan sounds like free software, and for a single-entity company with simple policies it often is. The bill shows up later, in seats once you need Premium controls, in foreign-currency card spend, and in contract terms signed with a vendor whose owner changed this year. Every Brex figure here comes from Brex's own pricing and support pages, re-checked on November 11, 2026, because vendor pricing pages change without notice.


***Key Takeaways***


-


Seat count sets the Brex subscription bill, and card spend doesn't, so model Premium at your real headcount before you sign.


-


Multiple expense policies, more than two entities, and customizable ERP and HRIS integrations sit on Premium, which is what usually moves a growing company off the free plan.


-


Brex says it charges no transaction fee to send ACH, wires, or checks, but card purchases in a foreign currency carry an FX markup.


-


Capital One now owns Brex, so price protection, roadmap commitments, and data export terms belong in the contract.


-


A rebate-funded commercial card program runs the math the other way, paying money back on spend instead of charging per seat.


## What does Brex pricing look like by plan?


Brex lists four options, two with published per-user prices and two quoted by its sales team. The table below shows each one as Brex listed it.

"Custom pricing" means a sales conversation. Entity count, card volume, and the implementation help you want will drive the quote, and the number is negotiated rather than read off a page. Ask for the per-user figure, the annual total, and the term length in writing.


### What does Brex Essentials include for $0?


Essentials includes bill pay, real-time reporting, and one local card program at no per-user charge. For a single-entity company with one expense policy, that covers issuing cards, watching spend as it happens, and paying bills from one account.


Card programs earn interchange on every swipe, which is how a $0 software tier can exist at all. Automated categorization helps with visibility, but automated coding still needs a person doing[credit card reconciliation](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/credit-card-reconciliation-software) at month-end.


### What does Brex Premium add for $12 per user?


Premium adds the controls a company needs once it spends money in more than one way. The headline additions are multiple customizable expense policies and advanced approvals, plus multi-entity support for US and international companies. Brex also lists live budgets, VAT documentation, and advanced travel rules on this tier, along with customizable ERP and HRIS integrations.


Live budgets and approval chains are usually the features finance teams notice first. They decide whether a policy breach turns up in the monthly close or gets stopped at the point of sale, and that's the same logic behind any well-built set of[card controls and spend policies](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/card-controls-spend-policies) .


### When does a company need Brex Enterprise?


Enterprise makes sense when the constraint is entity count instead of headcount. Brex lists unlimited entities and a named account manager on the Enterprise tier, both of which matter to a group with a dozen subsidiaries. Compare the custom quote with Premium at your seat count plus the cost of managing extra entities by hand.


## What does Brex cost at 25, 100, and 250 users?


At Premium's listed $12 per user a month, Brex costs $300 a month at 25 users, $1,200 at 100 users, and $3,000 at 250 users. Essentials stays at $0 at every size.

Card spend and payment volume don't move this line. A company putting $2 million a year on Brex cards pays the same subscription as one putting $200,000 on them, as long as the user count matches. So the user count is the variable to model, and I'd ask early how Brex defines a billable user, since an employee who only uploads receipts or an approver who never swipes a card may or may not count.


### Which features push a growing company off the free plan?


Most companies move to Premium because their structure changed. The usual triggers look like this.


-


A second expense policy, such as separate rules for field staff and head office


-


More than two legal entities, in the US or abroad, that each need their own books


-


ERP or HRIS integrations that need custom field mapping


-


Approval chains that change with amount, department, or merchant


-


Budgets that block spend before it happens instead of reporting it afterward


-


VAT documentation for reclaiming tax on international expenses


The ERP item tends to catch teams off guard. A company running NetSuite or Sage Intacct with departments, classes, and locations usually wants card transactions coded to those dimensions before they reach the ledger, and that kind of customizable integration sits on the paid tier.


### How does Brex's per-seat model compare with Ramp's?


Ramp lists a $0 tier, Ramp Plus at $15 per user per month plus a platform fee based on team size, and custom Enterprise pricing, as listed on Ramp's pricing page on November 11, 2026. Brex Premium is lower on the published seat price, but Ramp doesn't publish its platform fee, so a fair comparison needs written quotes from both.

BILL Spend & Expense, the product formerly called Divvy, also lists $0 per user per month on BILL's pricing page. Free entry tiers are now common across[expense management software](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/best-expense-management-software) , which makes the paid tier's triggers a better basis for comparison than the headline price.


## Does Brex charge fees beyond the plan price?


Yes, mainly on foreign-currency card spend. Brex says it doesn't charge transaction fees on outgoing wires, domestic or international, or on ACH payments and checks, though intermediary or recipient banks may charge their own fees on a wire.


That no-fee policy is generous next to what payments cost to run in-house. According to[AFP's 2022 Payments Cost Benchmarking Survey](https://www.financialprofessionals.org/about/learn-more/press-releases/Details/survey-73-of-organizations-are-transitioning-their-business-to-business-payments-from-checks-to-digital-payments) , issuing a paper check cost a median $2 to $4 and an ACH payment $0.26 to $0.50, and those are 2022 numbers. Nacha's[January 2026 volume report](https://www.nacha.org/news/same-day-ach-and-business-business-payments-propel-ach-network-volume-growth-2025) says the ACH Network carried about 8.1 billion B2B payments in 2025, up about 10%.


A free check is still a check, though. According to AFP's[2025 Payments Fraud and Control Survey](https://truist.com/content/dam/truist-bank/us/en/documents/info/cci/2025-afp-payments-fraud-control-survey-report-key-highlights.pdf) , 63% of organizations saw attempted or actual check fraud in 2024, against 21% for corporate or commercial cards and 5% for virtual cards. That gap is the case for[single-use cards](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/single-use-cards-fraud-prevention) on supplier payments, and Corpay issues single-use virtual cards where each number is good for one payment.


### Which Brex fees apply to foreign-currency card spend?


Brex applies an FX markup of up to 3% to card transactions that need currency conversion, according to its "Cost of Brex services" support page. Domestic card transactions carry no added fee.


The markup adds up faster than seat fees for some companies. Applied in full, Brex's listed markup would add as much as $1,500 a month to $50,000 of monthly foreign-currency card spend. Ask Brex for the actual markup on your currencies and put it in the contract.


### Are there minimums or balance requirements?


Brex's pricing page and fee page list no minimum balance or monthly account fee as of November 11, 2026. Eligibility is a separate question, and it's worth getting in writing.


In June 2022, Brex told tens of thousands of small-business customers it would stop serving them, according to[Banking Dive](https://www.bankingdive.com/news/fintech-brex-reputation-hit-after-dropping-small-business-customers/636097/) . It kept companies with equity funding, more than $1 million in revenue, more than 50 employees, or more than $500,000 in cash. A vendor that has redrawn its customer line once can do it again, and that risk deserves a contract clause now that a bank sets the strategy.


## What has changed since Brex got a new owner?


Capital One now owns Brex. It[announced the deal](https://capitalone.com/about/newsroom/capital-one-to-acquire-brex/) on January 22, 2026, in a stock-and-cash transaction valued at $5.15 billion, and[completed the acquisition](https://www.capitalone.com/about/newsroom/capital-one-completes-acquisition-of-brex/) on April 7, 2026, with Pedro Franceschi continuing as Brex's CEO.


At the close,[American Banker reported](https://www.americanbanker.com/payments/news/capital-one-closes-brex-acquisition) the deal as half cash and half stock, with Capital One planning to spend nearly $1 billion over three years on integration and expenses such as retention pay. Brex's pricing page didn't mention Capital One when we checked it on November 11, 2026.


A new owner doesn't rewrite your contract, but it does decide what happens at renewal. Ask for these four things in writing.


1.


Price protection for the full term, with a cap on per-user increases at renewal


2.


Roadmap commitments for the features you're buying, such as multi-entity support and ERP integrations


3.


The support model after integration, including whether your named contact stays


4.


Data export at exit, in a format your ERP and auditors can use, with a defined window after termination


None of this assumes prices will rise. Nobody outside Capital One knows whether Brex's plans will change, and an integration budget that size could point toward investment as easily as toward repricing. The contract is the only part of that you control.


## Is Brex worth it compared with a rebate-funded card program?


Brex is probably worth it for a funded company with a simple entity structure, since Essentials costs nothing. The math changes once you're paying for seats, because a rebate-funded commercial card program runs the other direction and pays money back on spend.


Rebates come from interchange, the fee a supplier's bank pays the card issuer on each transaction, and the issuer shares part of it with the company running the program. According to Visa's 2026[USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees](https://usa.visa.com/content/dam/VCOM/download/merchants/visa-usa-interchange-reimbursement-fees.pdf) schedule, supplier interchange on Visa commercial cards runs 2.70% plus $0.10 for card-not-present transactions and 1.30% plus $35 at the large-ticket rate. In its[Fiscal 2025 Annual Report](https://annualreport.visa.com/chairman-and-ceo-message/) , Visa says it holds about 40% of commercial card payments and sizes B2B, P2P, and other flows at about $200 trillion a year.


### Who is Brex's pricing a good fit for?


Brex's pricing suits companies that can live on Essentials, and some can for a long time. The clearest fits are below.


-


Venture-funded companies with one entity and one expense policy


-


Teams that want cards, bill pay, and reimbursements in one app with no software line item


-


Companies whose card spend is mostly employee travel and software rather than supplier invoices


For those companies, card management with built-in expense tracking is hard to beat at $0. Companies that need large monthly limits for vendor payments should compare Brex's quote with[high-limit business credit cards](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/high-limit-business-credit-cards) .


### When does a rebate-funded program cost less?


A rebate-funded program can cost less once you're on Premium and a large share of your spend goes to suppliers. Seat fees grow with headcount, while rebates grow with spend.


Supplier acceptance is moving in the right direction. According to Mastercard's 2025[commercial card acceptance](https://newsroom.mastercard.com/news/perspectives/2025/commercial-card-acceptance/) research, card-accepting suppliers are 14 percentage points more likely to say they're very efficient at maximizing working capital. Corpay's card programs generate $800M+ in rebates per year for clients, paid out of the same supplier spend a per-seat platform charges you to manage. The honest caveat is that rebates depend on which suppliers take cards, so compare[commercial card programs](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/best-commercial-card) on rebate terms against your actual vendor file.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much does Brex cost per month?


Brex Essentials is $0 per user a month and Premium is $12 per user a month, as listed on November 11, 2026. Enterprise and Smart Card are custom-priced.


### Is Brex really free?


The Essentials software tier is free, with no per-user charge for bill pay, real-time reporting, and one local card program. Costs appear when you need Premium features, such as multiple expense policies or more than two entities, and when you spend in foreign currencies.


### When should a company upgrade to Brex Premium?


Upgrade when you need more than one expense policy, US and international entities, live budgets, advanced approvals, VAT documentation, or customizable ERP and HRIS integrations. Each sits on Premium at the listed per-user price, so model it at your full user count.


### Does Brex charge for ACH, wires, or checks?


Brex says it charges no transaction fees to send domestic wires, international wires, ACH, or checks from a Brex business account. Intermediary banks that route a wire, and the recipient's bank, may still charge their own fees, which Brex doesn't control.


### Who owns Brex now?


Capital One owns Brex. It announced the deal in January 2026 and completed it on April 7, 2026, with Pedro Franceschi continuing as CEO. Brex's pricing page still carries Brex branding and didn't mention Capital One as of November 11, 2026.


### Is Brex better than Amex?


Neither is better across the board. Brex bundles cards with expense and bill-pay software, while Amex competes mainly on the cards themselves. Start with whether you want a[charge card or a credit card](https://www.corpay.com/resources/blog/charge-card-vs-credit-card) , then compare rewards, acceptance, and the software around the card.
